item.title: WATCH: Global News Hour at 6 BC: Feb. 20
item.description: Watch the online edition of Global News Hour at 6 BC.

item.title: Public consultations underway on future of Alberta’s Fortress Mountain Resort
item.description: Public consultations are underway over plans to develop Fortress Mountain, a former ski hill in Alberta's Kananaskis Country, west of Calgary, into an all-season resort.

item.title: Saskatchewan dancers head to Dublin for Dance World Cup, representing Canada
item.description: Young dancers from Saskatchewan are getting ready to head out for The Dance World Cup in Dublin, July 8-18. Dancers say they are excited to represent Canada.

item.title: Nurses discouraged from working at Winnipeg hospital due to safety concerns
item.description: Nurses at Manitoba's second-largest hospital have declared it too dangerous to work in and are discouraging union members from accepting jobs or shifts there.

item.title: Dr. Joss Reimer says misinformation a key target as she becomes Canada’s top doctor
item.description: Tackling health misinformation and rebuilding public trust are top priorities for Canada's incoming chief public health officer Dr. Joss Reimer.

item.title: City of Kelowna security patrols should be expanded to Rutland, business owners say
item.description: On Thursday, the City of Kelowna announced its latest response to the ongoing issues plaguing downtown: temporary overnight security patrols.

item.title: Montreal promises new approach to homeless with encampment ‘tolerance zones’
item.description: The city said its new policy creates 'tolerance zones' on city-owned land, where encampments would be permitted if they meet certain safety rules.

item.title: Barrie Colts win their 9th straight game 5-1 over the London Knights
item.description: The Colts are now 20-1-1 in their last 22 games and have won nine straight games.

item.title: Trump keeps carveout under CUSMA in new 10 per cent global tariff
item.description: A fact sheet from the White House said the latest tariff will not hit goods compliant under the Canada-U.S.-Mexico agreement on trade, known as CUSMA.

item.title: Board of Metro Vancouver’s CAO tight-lipped about status, cost of ‘leak’ investigation
item.description: The Chief Administrative Officer of Metro Vancouver has spoken for the first time since Global News broke the story about chaos in the organization's leadership.
